title: A protocol to enrich in undifferentiated cells from neuroblastoma tumor tissue samples and cell lines
protocol: Aspirate media from a tissue culture flask with SK-N-SH cells.
Gently wash the cells twice with PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+, using 3 mL for a 25 cm2 cell culture flask.
Aspirate PBS and add Versene to cover the cell layer, using 500 μL for a 25 cm2 cell culture flask.
Incubate at 37°C in the cell incubator for 5 minutes.
Stop the dissociation by adding 2 mL of FACS medium.
Resuspend cells by pipetting up-and-down until a homogeneous cell suspension is achieved.
Transfer the cell suspension to a sterile 15 mL plastic tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of FACS medium gently pipetting up and down.
Pass through a sterile cell strainer with 40 μm pore size into a sterile 50 mL tube to remove non-dissociated cell aggregates.
Count the number of cells in the suspension using trypan blue for viability calculation.
Prepare a suspension of at least 1 × 10^6 cells per 100–200 mL of FACS medium for labelling.
Prepare also a suspension of at least 2 × 10^4 cells for unlabeled cells and 2 × 10^4 cells for cells to be labelled only with secondary antibody as controls.
Incubate sample cell suspension with 1 μg of CD44 primary antibody for 40–60 min on ice.
Wash cells 3 times with 1 mL cold FACS medium with gentle centrifugation (5 min at 300 g and 4°C) between washes.
Incubate on ice for 30 min with Alexa488-donkey-α-mouse at a 1:500 dilution in a volume of 200 μL.
Wash cells 3 times with 1 mL cold FACS medium with gentle centrifugation (5 min at 300 g and 4°C) between washes.
Pass the cell suspension through a 50 μm cell strainer before sorting.
Seed 1 × 10^5 of recovered sorted cells per well in a 6-well ultralow binding plate with 2 mL of pre-warmed NCM.
Transfer the 6-well plate to a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator overnight (6–18 h).
Obtain a homogeneous single cell suspension.
Observe under the microscope and recover all previously sorted cells from the ultralow binding plate.
Pass through a sterile cell strainer with 40 μm pore size to remove possible aggregates.
Alternatively, dissociate aggregates by resuspending in Versene after gentle centrifugation.
Centrifuge again and recover cells in NCM media.
Count the number of cells in the suspension.
Calculate viability by mixing a small aliquot with an equal volume of trypan blue.
Use manual or automatic cell counting for accurate quantification.
Ensure you have a single cell suspension by imaging.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed NCM per well in a 6-well ultralow binding plate.
Mix the cell suspension a few times by pipetting before plating.
Pipette a volume of cell suspension so that the final concentration is 1–2.5 cells/μL (2,500–5,000 cells in 2 mL of media) per well.
Ensure even distribution of the cells in the well by slowly moving the plate drawing a cross and by gentle tapping.
Transfer the 6-well plate to a 37°C cell incubator for 7 days.
Ensure even distribution of cells in each well to maintain clonality and tumor sphere growth.
Maintain the plate flat throughout the incubation period without moving or removing it from the incubator.
Dissociate tumorspheres after 7 days for imaging and collection.
Observe the plate under a microscope to confirm dispersed cell spheres.
Gently rotate the plate in circles to concentrate the tumorspheres in the middle of each well.
Take images of the resulting tumorspheres to quantify their number and diameter.
Transfer all tumorspheres from the well using a 10 μL pipette into a sterile plastic tube containing 500 μL 0.05% trypsin, ensuring minimal medium volume is transferred.
If different wells with the same condition are used, combine tumorspheres into a single well to minimize recovery volume.
Alternatively, transfer tumorspheres to a solution with a cocktail of enzymes for better dissociation, especially if spheres come from primary tissue.
Keep the plate open for the shortest time possible to avoid contamination.
Gently pipette the tumorspheres in the trypsin solution from time to time to help dissociation.
Incubate the tumorspheres with the trypsin solution for approximately 5 minutes at room temperature.
Collect the tumorspheres by transferring the media containing cells into a 15 mL falcon tube.
Allow the spheres to settle by gravity sedimentation for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving about 200 μL in the falcon tube to avoid aspirating the tumorsphere.
Add 1 mL of 0.05% trypsin to the tumorspheres and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Stop the trypsinization by adding 2 mL of NCM.
Transfer the cell suspension to a sterile 15 mL plastic tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL of NCM gently pipetting up and down.
Pass the cell suspension through a sterile cell strainer with a 40 μm pore size to remove non-dissociated cell aggregates.
Count the number of cells in the suspension using Trypan blue for viability calculation.
Reseed tumorspheres following step 6 to have secondary tumorspheres.
Image and collect secondary tumorspheres following step 7.
Dissociate cells and plate to form tertiary tumorspheres following the procedure described in step 8.
Image and collect tertiary tumorspheres following step 7.
Dissociate tertiary tumorspheres following steps 8.a to f.
Use dissociated cells for characterization, functional assays, or single cell experiments.
Seed tertiary tumorspheres on a tissue culture treated surface for them to adhere after a short incubation time.
Characterize the cells in spheres by immunofluorescence, video-microscopy, or differentiation.
Include fresh spheres in optimal cutting temperature compound and cryopreserve as frozen blocks.
Slice frozen blocks using a cryotome to assess composition by immunofluorescence.
Set a cryopreservation container filled with propan-2-ol aside, at 20°C–25°C.
Dissociate tumorspheres into cell suspension as in step 8.a to f.
Prepare enough cryopreservation media.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of cryopreservation media after centrifugation, mixing gently.
Transfer the cell suspension to a labelled 1.5–2 mL cryovial and place it in the container.
Place the cryovial with cells into a −80°C freezer.
Transfer cryovials into a liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage the day after.
Pre-warm NCM at room temperature, then place it under the tissue-culture hood.
Place the cryovial containing frozen undifferentiated cells in a 37°C water bath for 1–2 minutes, or until fully thawed.
Transfer all medium with cells from the cryovial into a 15 mL sterile tube containing 1 mL of NCM.
Sequentially add NCM to double the current volume, gently agitating and incubating briefly after each addition to gradually dilute DMSO.
Repeat until reaching 10 mL of media.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of NCM.
Plate cells for tumorsphere formation after thawing.
Let the plated cells recover to conserve their undifferentiated character.
